Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Giles Snyder. Democrats have won control of the U.S.
Senate, flipping six Republican-held seats in tonight's midterm elections. The latest pickup
is in Iowa as votes continue to be counted in key congressional races across the country. NPR's
Windsor Johnston is in the studio with the latest. Hi, Windsor.
Hi, Giles. Well, Democrats have now flipped six Republican-held Senate seats,
including, as you just said, a victory in Iowa, where Democrat Josh Turek has defeated Republican
Ashley Hinson. In Texas, Democratic State Representative James Talerigo
defeated Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton, who's a close ally of President Trump. Democrats
have also picked up seats in Kansas, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Ohio. On the House side,
Democrats have flipped 11 Republican-held seats, including in Pennsylvania, New Jersey,
North Carolina, and Kentucky. And the Democratic victories come on a night when
rising prices in Iran have really weighed heavily on voters, and the cost of living was a major
concern. And many voters expressed dissatisfaction with the direction of the country. We've also
heard from President Trump tonight. In a post on Truth Social, he wrote that Republicans would
have won in a landslide if his name had been on the ballot. Among the multiple House seats
Democrats have flipped is in New Jersey. Mike Hayes, a member station WNYC, has more.
First-time Democratic nominee Rebecca Bennett has defeated incumbent Republican Tom Kane, Jr.
in New Jersey's hotly contested 7th congressional district. 39-year-old Bennett is a former Navy
helicopter pilot and healthcare executive. She ran as a centrist in the moderate New Jersey swing
district. Kane was seeking a third term amidst a year filled with personal challenges. In March,
Kane went mysteriously missing from Congress for over 100 days. He later said he was suffering
from depression and had been hospitalized. For NPR, I'm Mike Hayes in Mt. Laurel.
In Texas, Republican Governor Greg Abbott has conceded to Democrat Gina Hinoza.
After looking at all the details of every county in the entire state, I made the decision to go
ahead and call Gina Hinoza and congratulate her on winning this race for governor of the state of
Texas. Hinoza's victory makes her the first Democrat elected governor of Texas since
Ann Richards in 1990. In Wisconsin, the Associated Press has called the race for governor. For
Democrat David Crowley, he will be Wisconsin's first black governor. In other races, the AP
is called the contest in Ohio for Democrat Amy Acton over Republican Vivek Ramaswamy.
And in Florida, Republican Congressman Byron Donalds defeated Democrat David Jolly.
And you're listening to NPR News. Despite a heated campaign cycle,
and Michigan voters say they want people to set aside their differences after the election
from member station WKAR Sophia Salovey had reports. Michigan has remained deeply purple
in 2026 with party division crossing towns, neighborhoods, and even households.
Elise Mitchell, a Democrat, got emotional as she talked about the future of the country
outside her polling place in Grand Ledge. People are focusing more on what's separating us than
how we could actually find solutions. First-time voter and Mason resident Cara Woods says she leans
conservative Republican. Woods is pregnant and has been thinking about how she'll talk to her
children about these divisions. We'll teach them and raise them to respect each other no matter
what everyone's views are. Woods and Mitchell aren't alone. Many voters across the political
spectrum were eager for people to get along after the election. I'm Sophia Salovey in Mid-Michigan.
An inmate who escaped from a Tennessee prison has been recaptured. Authorities say Jacob Morley
was apprehended Tuesday near Kansas City with troopers using roadside cameras and a helicopter
to tracking down. Morley escaped from Tennessee's northwest correctional complex more than a week
ago. He was handed a life sentence for killing a co-worker four years ago. Several flights in Europe
received hoax of bomb threats Tuesday. No injuries reported. None of the planes had to make emergency
landings. The hoax threats came a day after a plane headed for Bulgaria was diverted to Hungary
after receiving a similar threat while in the air. I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR News.
